facts.text: Administrator consent to delegated permissions does not grant ChatGPT an administrator role; delegated permissions act on behalf of the signed-in user and are constrained by that user's privileges.
Delegated Files.Read.All and Sites.Read.All permissions allow ChatGPT to read files and sites accessible to the authenticated user, but do not provide tenant-wide application-level access.

Microsoft recommends restricting user consent to selected permissions and verified publishers, reviewing all permission requests centrally, and verifying the publisher and requested permissions before tenant-wide consent.

Microsoft Entra consent and ChatGPT action enablement are separate steps; consent alone does not enable ChatGPT actions or connect individual accounts, and existing Microsoft access restrictions still apply.

recommendations: Review the exact permissions requested and verify they align with the business need before granting consent.
Implement an administrator approval workflow for permission requests to ensure centralized review and control.
Restrict user consent to verified publishers and selected permissions to reduce risk of excessive access.
Monitor granted permissions and review existing app permissions regularly, depending on licensing capabilities.
unknowns: Whether the requested delegated permissions have been reviewed and authorized by an administrator in this tenant.
Whether the ChatGPT application is a verified publisher in the tenant's Microsoft Entra configuration.
Exact controls available in the Business plan for monitoring and restricting delegated permissions for ChatGPT.
risks: Granting delegated Files.Read.All and Sites.Read.All permissions allows ChatGPT to access all files and sites the signed-in user can access, which may include confidential or personal data, posing a data exposure risk if misused.
If administrator consent is granted without proper review, excessive permissions may be granted leading to potential overexposure of sensitive data.
Lack of monitoring or review of granted permissions could allow unnoticed privilege creep or unauthorized access.

controls.action: Implement an administrator approval workflow for all permission consent requests.
controls.location: Microsoft Entra admin center under Enterprise applications > User consent settings (verification required).
controls.prerequisites: Administrator role with consent management privileges; appropriate licensing for consent workflows (verification required).
controls.verification: Confirm that all permission requests require administrator approval before consent is granted.
controls.rollback: Revoke consent for ChatGPT application permissions if unauthorized permissions were granted.

controls.action: Restrict user consent to selected permissions and verified publishers only.
controls.location: Microsoft Entra admin center > User settings > User consent settings (verification required).
controls.prerequisites: Administrator role; tenant configured to restrict user consent.
controls.verification: Verify user consent restrictions are enabled and enforced.
controls.rollback: Adjust user consent settings to allow broader consent if business needs change.

controls.action: Regularly review granted permissions and connected applications for ChatGPT.
controls.location: Microsoft Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > Permissions (verification required).
controls.prerequisites: Administrator role with access to application permissions reports.
controls.verification: Audit permissions granted to ChatGPT and verify alignment with business requirements.
controls.rollback: Revoke unnecessary permissions or disconnect ChatGPT application if risks are identified.

plan_guidance.text: The Business plan may have limited monitoring capabilities; verify available controls for permission review and consent management in this plan.

evidence.text: Microsoft Entra consent and ChatGPT action enablement are separate steps, potentially performed by different administrators. Consent does not automatically connect individual accounts or enable actions. Existing Microsoft access restrictions still apply. Sites.Selected is not supported for live SharePoint search; supported ChatGPT site-collection restrictions are a separate mechanism.

evidence.section: Overview; Connect SharePoint; Review permissions for live SharePoint access

evidence.text: Microsoft permission grants, enabled ChatGPT actions and an individual's account connection are distinct prerequisites. A change to the Microsoft grant can require reviewing or refreshing the connection.
evidence.title: Workspace app controls and plan distinctions
evidence.section: Default behavior by plan; Role-based access control; Manage plugin and app access

evidence.text:
Microsoft recommends restricting user consent to selected permissions and verified publishers, with other requests reviewed centrally. An administrator approval workflow can support this process. Review existing apps and granted permissions; additional monitoring capabilities depend on licensing.

Before tenant-wide consent, verify the publisher and application identity, understand every requested permission, and match the request to the expected business functionality. Familiarity or widespread use is not sufficient justification. Do not grant permissions that are unexplained or appear excessive; obtain clarification from the publisher.
evidence.title: Evaluating application consent requests
evidence.section: Auditing and monitoring; Evaluate a request for tenant-wide admin consent

evidence.text: Where appropriate, consider user assignment restrictions for approved applications. Review delegated versus application permissions explicitly rather than assuming all consent requests have the same impact.
evidence.title: Evaluating application consent requests
evidence.section: Auditing and monitoring; Evaluate a request for tenant-wide admin consent

evidence.text:
Delegated access acts for an authenticated user. Both the application's granted scopes and the user's own authorization constrain access. Delegated Files.Read.All permits reading files accessible to that user.

Application permissions operate as the application without a signed-in user. The same permission name can have different implications: application Files.Read.All allows reading tenant files through Microsoft Graph. Application permissions and some privileged delegated scopes need administrator consent.

evidence.text: Consent authorizes specified permissions. An administrator can approve delegated permissions too, so the administrator's participation alone does not establish that the app has application-only access or an administrator role. Inspect the permission type and requested operations.

grounding_reason: All factual claims in the assessment are directly supported by the cited evidence chunks. The assessment correctly distinguishes delegated permissions from administrator roles, aligns with Microsoft's recommendations on consent review and approval workflows, and notes the separation of consent and ChatGPT action enablement. The recommendations and controls are clearly conditional and based on the evidence. No invented capabilities, pricing, or guarantees are asserted. Unknowns are properly identified as missing information.
